description: Move the low-rank path A@Omega range-finder matvec and the A@Q Rayleigh matvec from FP32-SIMT to 3xTF32 tensor cores. brief-44 won by moving the CQR2 Gram + Vd lift to 3xTF32 but explicitly LEFT these A@Q / A@Omega matvecs on FP32-SIMT (~40 TFLOPS) -- they are big n-by-n times n-by-k GEMMs that on B200 tensor cores run ~8-10x faster, and 3xTF32 Ozaki keeps FP32 accuracy so the orth gate stays clean (plain TF32 trips it -> fallback, per brief-44/45). Work-reduction via faster hardware units, not re-implementing a kernel. Targets low-rank shapes 3/8/10 and the mixed-peel low-rank subset (shape 6). Pure torch.

KEEPER HEAD=7f70a1fe (geomean matched-clean 30927-30938 vs parent 31126, -0.6%). 39/39 valid, 0 new fallback, stream=0. CENTRAL FINDING (brief premise CORRECTED): the four low-rank A@X matvecs (A@Omega/A@Qd power/A@Qd Rayleigh/A@Vc) were NOT on FP32-SIMT -- they were ALREADY plain single-pass TF32 tensor cores (plain torch.bmm inside the _LR_TF32 allow_tf32=True scope). Proof: t2 forced explicit tf32 = geomean 31198 == parent recorded 31127. So the real lever is 1-pass TF32 (fastest) vs 3-pass FP32-accurate 3xTF32 (~1.7x GEMM cost). WIN: per-shape _lr_av_mode_for routes 3xTF32 ONLY for the n=1024 near-rank case (k>=768 = shape10 nearrank1024): shape10 102783->94084us (-8.6%), the ONLY shape that moves; every other shape within +-0.2%. Mechanism is NOT fallback (reseed sweep: tf32 3/300, 3xtf32 5/300 -- both ~fallback-free on shape10; on the actual bench seed 770005 3xtf32 has MORE fallback, 3 vs 0) -- it is a cutlass kernel-SELECTION effect: the 1024x1024@1024x768 batched GEMM at k=768 hits a faster tiling under 3xTF32's hi/lo split than the 1-pass TF32 pick. Shapes 3/4/8/12 all measured FASTER on plain tf32 (3xtf32's extra passes cost more where gate-clean) -> kept on tf32; shape3 (brief's zero-margin concern) stays gate-clean across 5 reseeds, unchanged from parent. REFUTED: (t1) all-shapes 3xTF32 REGRESSES (31616, shapes 3/4 slower); (t4) 3xTF32 on the Qd-projection GEMMs R<-R-Qd(Qd^T R) is NET-NEUTRAL (30959 vs 30938) -- confirms parent's t9 (projections too small to amortize Ozaki at b640/b60), reverted to fp32. OPEN DIRECTIONS: (1) The persistent FP32-SIMT simt_sgemm in the shape8 profile (~11%: Qd-projections + complement CQR2 trsm) is real remaining SIMT work but 3xTF32 on the projection GEMMs specifically was net-neutral -- a FUSED complement-build kernel (project + CQR in one launch, like brief-51's CQR2 fusion idea) might capture it where the split-GEMM cannot. (2) The k=768 cutlass-tiling win suggests probing whether OTHER large-k GEMMs elsewhere (e.g. the k=608 dense1024 dominant Gram, or shape5/7 large-n paths) hit the same bad 1-pass-TF32 tiling that a hi/lo split fixes -- a targeted 3xTF32-or-explicit-tiling probe. (3) shape10's dominant cost is the mega_eigh_clust_split_k inner solve (64%) -- out of this brief's matvec scope but the real prize; a kernel brief (like brief-35/50) owns it. (4) A 2-term (not 3-term) hi/lo split on the shape10 A@X might hit the same good tiling at lower cost -- untested micro-lever.
